questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(1). Making room for others to travel safely is also a social responsibility.
questions.question: When using the road, watch what pedestrians and vehicles around you are doing and travel with consideration for their position.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(2). The ban on noisy driving puts this into concrete form.
questions.question: Do not think only of your own convenience in travelling; take care not to trouble people living along the road with unpleasant noise and the like.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(4). It is one of a driver's social responsibilities.
questions.question: When you see someone in trouble from a traffic accident or a breakdown, help each other out by calling for help or giving aid.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(6) such a vehicle may have no driver aboard and may stop suddenly on the road.
questions.question: An automated vehicle under specified automated operation always has a driver aboard.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 1 item 2(3) a driver is to acquire the knowledge needed for emergency first aid as a precaution.
questions.question: Knowledge of emergency first aid is for ambulance crews; a driver need not acquire it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). A specified small motorized bicycle is treated the same way.
questions.question: On a green light a light road vehicle may go straight on and turn left, and to turn right it may go straight to the turning point and change direction there.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). That is the only exception, and being in a hurry is not a reason.
questions.question: On an amber light a vehicle must not proceed beyond the stopping position, but if it was already close to that position when the light changed and cannot stop safely, it may carry on.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(1). A pedestrian who has not yet started must not begin crossing.
questions.question: On an amber light a pedestrian already crossing must finish the crossing promptly or give it up and turn back.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) a specified small motorized bicycle or light road vehicle may only go straight on and turn left, and turns right by going straight to the turning point and changing direction there.
questions.question: On a green light every vehicle may go straight on, turn left and turn right.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Appendix 1(1) you may carry on only when you are close to the stopping position and cannot stop safely.
questions.question: On an amber light you may carry on if you are in a hurry, even before you have entered the intersection.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a). At the same moment it means a red light for traffic crossing that direction.
questions.question: When a police officer raises an arm horizontally to the side, that has the same meaning as a green light for traffic running parallel to the front of their body.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 1(3)(a). You read a hand signal by reference to which way the officer is facing.
questions.question: When a police officer raises an arm horizontally to the side, that has the same meaning as a red light for traffic crossing the direction parallel to the front of their body.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 3 item 1 the signal of the officer or traffic warden prevails in that case.
questions.question: Where a police officer's hand signal differs from the traffic light, you may simply follow the light.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 3 item 2 the officer's instruction prevails.
questions.question: Where a police officer's instruction differs from the regulation shown by a road sign, you must follow the sign.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 4. There are rules that bind people who are not driving as well.
questions.question: You must not ask a person without a licence, or a person who has been drinking, to drive a vehicle.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 5. The person serving the drink carries responsibility too.
questions.question: You must not serve alcohol to, or press it on, a person who is about to drive.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 1(4) forbids scattering or dumping dirty water, rubbish, nails, glass fragments and the like at all, with no exception for clearing up later.
questions.question: Scattering glass fragments on the road is acceptable as long as you mean to clear them up straight afterwards.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 1 Section 4 item 6 also prohibits selling or handing over goods that would overload the vehicle.
questions.question: You must not ask a driver to drive overloaded, but selling goods that would overload the vehicle is not prohibited.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 2 item 3. This is the exception to the rule of keeping right.
questions.question: Even on a road with neither a sidewalk nor a side strip (路側帯) of sufficient width, you may walk on the left-hand edge where keeping right would mean crossing back and forth and so be more dangerous.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 2 item 4. Even a pedestrian-only road is not entirely free of vehicles.
questions.question: On a pedestrian-only road a pedestrian may walk down the middle, but should take care because vehicles with permission do use it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 2(3). If you are already crossing, finish promptly or turn back.
questions.question: A flashing green on a pedestrian signal means the same as an amber light, and once it starts flashing you must not begin crossing.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 2(5). A scramble crossing turns every vehicle signal red and lets pedestrians move freely.
questions.question: A pedestrian must not cross a road diagonally, but at a scramble crossing you may cross diagonally in accordance with the pedestrian signal.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 2 item 1 you must use the sidewalk where there is one, except where road works or the like make it impassable.
questions.question: Even on a road with a sidewalk you may walk on the roadway if it is easier going.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 2 item 3 a pedestrian must walk on the right-hand edge.
questions.question: On a road with neither a sidewalk nor a side strip (路側帯) of sufficient width, a pedestrian must walk on the left-hand edge.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 1 you must cross at the crossing where one is nearby.
questions.question: Even with a pedestrian crossing nearby you may cross anywhere as long as no vehicle is coming.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 2 Section 3 item 2(3) a flashing green means the same as an amber light, and you must not begin crossing.
questions.question: A flashing green on a pedestrian signal means the same as a steady green.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 1 item 1(3) and (4). The age limit binds not only the rider but also the person lending the vehicle.
questions.question: A specified small motorized bicycle (e-scooter, etc.) must not carry two people, and must not be lent to anyone under 16.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 1 item 1(8) asks riders to make an effort to wear a safety helmet; it does not say that riding without one is not allowed.
questions.question: You must wear a safety helmet to ride a specified small motorized bicycle (e-scooter, etc.), and anyone not wearing one may not ride.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 2 item 2(1). Do not ride a bicycle that does not fit you.
questions.question: Check that the bicycle saddle is fixed in place and set so that the toes of both feet reach the ground when you sit astride.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 2 item 2(6). You must not ride a bicycle whose brakes are faulty.
questions.question: Check that both the front and rear brakes work well on a bicycle, stopping it within 3 metres from 10 km/h.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 2 item 1(2) you must not ride a bicycle whose brakes are faulty.
questions.question: You may ride a bicycle with faulty brakes as long as you do not go fast.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 2 item 1(2) you must not ride a bicycle without a rear light or reflector at night.
questions.question: You may ride a bicycle without a rear light or reflector at night.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 3 item 1(4) it may travel only on a sidewalk carrying the road sign or road marking that permits exceptional specified small motorized bicycles and ordinary bicycles on the sidewalk.
questions.question: An exceptional specified small motorized bicycle may travel on any sidewalk as long as its maximum-speed indicator lamp is flashing.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 3 item 1(6), where there is a bicycle crossing nearby, the bicycle must use that bicycle crossing.
questions.question: When a bicycle is about to cross the road it may use either a nearby bicycle crossing or a pedestrian crossing, whichever it likes.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 3 item 1(1) an ordinary bicycle must use the bicycle path where there is one, except in cases such as road works.
questions.question: Where there is a bicycle path, an ordinary bicycle may still ride along the left edge of the roadway if the rider prefers.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 3 Section 3 item 2(8)(a) it must proceed slowly (徐行) at a speed from which it can stop at once.
questions.question: An ordinary bicycle on a sidewalk may ride on without slowing as long as there is no pedestrian.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 4 Section 1 item 1(1)(c). Driving in breach of a condition is a licence-condition offence.
questions.question: Before driving you check that you are meeting any conditions noted on your licence, such as the use of glasses.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 4 Section 1 item 1(1)(e). It has to be on both the front and the rear.
questions.question: A novice driver within one year of obtaining a semi-medium or ordinary licence must display the beginner's mark at the set positions on the front and the rear of the car.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 4 Section 1 item 1(2) asks such drivers to make an effort to display the mark; it does not say they may not drive without it.
questions.question: A driver aged 70 or over may not drive an ordinary car without displaying the older driver's mark.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 4 Section 1 item 2 you take a rest once every two hours.
questions.question: When you will be driving for a long time, take a rest once every four hours.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 4 Section 2. Driving during a suspension is treated as unlicensed driving.
questions.question: Even someone who holds a licence may not drive while it is suspended.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 4 Section 2 item 1. The three are divided by the purpose and setting of the driving.
questions.question: There are three kinds of driver's licence: Class 1, Class 2 and the provisional licence.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 4 Section 2 you must carry the licence with you when driving.
questions.question: As long as you hold a licence you may drive even with the licence itself left at home.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 4 Section 2 item 1(3) a Class 1 holder must have held it for three years or more.
questions.question: The instructor sitting beside a provisional-licence holder practising in an ordinary car need only have held a Class 1 licence for that vehicle for one year or more.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 1(1). That first small opening also serves as a signal to other traffic.
questions.question: When you open a door to get out, you first open it a little and pause, then get out once you have checked that it is safe.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 2(1). A relaxed, correct driving posture is the first step to safe driving.
questions.question: The fore-and-aft position of the seat is set so that your knee is slightly bent when the clutch is pressed down.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 3(1) the driver and passengers must wear seat belts even where airbags are fitted.
questions.question: In a car fitted with airbags the airbag protects the body, so seat belts need not be worn.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 1 item 3(1) passengers in the rear seats must wear them too.
questions.question: It is enough for the driver and the front-seat passenger to wear seat belts.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1. Only on a one-way road does this limit not apply, because there is no oncoming traffic.
questions.question: Except where the road is one way, when you cross onto the right-hand side of the road you must keep the amount you cross over as small as you can.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1(4). Without that marking you may not cross over, however similar the terrain.
questions.question: Where the Keep right road marking is in place near a bend on a steeply graded road, you may cross onto the right-hand side of the road.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. The exception in Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1(3) is limited to roads whose left-hand side is under 6 metres wide, and you may not cross over on a wider one.
questions.question: On a road with a clear view you may cross onto the right-hand side to overtake even where the left-hand side is 6 metres wide or more.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 2 item 1(3) you may not cross over where the No overtaking on the right-hand side of the road sign or marking is in place.
questions.question: On a road with a clear view whose left-hand side is under 6 metres wide, you may cross onto the right-hand side whenever it is for overtaking.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(3). Someone crossing from behind the stopped vehicle cannot be seen.
questions.question: When a vehicle is stopped at or just before a pedestrian crossing or a bicycle crossing, you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) before passing it and moving ahead of it.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(4). Not only overtaking, which involves changing course, but also passing without changing lanes is prohibited.
questions.question: Within a pedestrian crossing or a bicycle crossing and the 30 metres before it, you must not overtake another vehicle or pass it without changing lanes.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 2(2) you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) before the crossing, or before the stop line where there is one, and give way.
questions.question: When a pedestrian is about to cross at a pedestrian crossing, you must proceed slowly (徐行) and give way to them.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 3 item 7(2) allows leaving a safe clearance or proceeding slowly (徐行), and there is no exception that sounding the horn is enough.
questions.question: When passing a bicycle, even if you cannot leave a safe clearance, you may go by at the same speed as long as you sound the horn to warn the rider.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(2). Braking distance changes with the state of the road surface and the weight of the load.
questions.question: Braking distance becomes longer when you drive on a road wet with rain or when you are carrying a heavy load.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 4 item 2(3). When the road surface and the tyres are in poor condition you have to reduce speed accordingly.
questions.question: When the road is wet with rain and the tyres are worn, the stopping distance can stretch to about twice what it is on a dry road with tyres in good condition.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. That is the braking distance; reaction distance is what the vehicle travels between the driver sensing danger and the brakes actually beginning to work.
questions.question: Reaction distance is the distance the vehicle travels from the moment the brakes begin to work until it stops.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Article 11 of the Road Traffic Act Enforcement Order in force from 1 September 2026, the legal maximum speed for a car on such a road without a center line is 30 km/h.
questions.question: On an ordinary road with no center line and no vehicle lanes, a car may be driven at up to 60 km/h as long as no maximum speed is posted by road sign or road marking.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 3(3) you must move over as far as you can and then proceed slowly.
questions.question: For a turn to leave the road, moving to the edge or the centre is enough and no slowing (徐行) is required.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 7 item 3(1) requires proceeding slowly (徐行); a complete stop is required where the Stop sign stands and in similar cases.
questions.question: At an intersection without traffic control you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) where the crossing road is a priority road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(2). You either operate the left turn indicator or give a hand signal, such as raising the right forearm vertically at the elbow.
questions.question: The signal for leaving a roundabout is given when you have passed the side of the exit immediately before the one you intend to take.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 5 item 1(2). In every other case you signal when you have passed the side of the exit immediately before the one you intend to take.
questions.question: If you are taking the exit immediately after entering a roundabout, you give the signal at the moment you enter that roundabout.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Article 53 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act a signal is required at a roundabout when leaving and when proceeding slowly (徐行), stopping or reversing, and no signal is required on entry.
questions.question: When you are about to enter a roundabout you must signal with the left turn indicator.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(b). Your path and the other vehicle's would overlap.
questions.question: You must not overtake while the vehicle ahead is moving to the right in order to turn right or for a similar reason.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(d). If you change course you risk striking the vehicle behind.
questions.question: You must not overtake while the vehicle behind is overtaking you.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(2)(a) double overtaking is prohibited as dangerous, and the width of the road is irrelevant.
questions.question: Even while the vehicle ahead is overtaking a car, you may overtake if the road is wide.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 6 item 1(3)(e) the distance is 30 metres before the intersection.
questions.question: At an intersection and within the 10 metres before it you must not change course to overtake.

questions.explanation: This is Article 37-2 paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Road Traffic Act. You must proceed slowly when entering, and vehicles already travelling inside the roundabout have priority.
questions.question: When you are about to enter a roundabout you must proceed slowly (徐行) and must not obstruct the progress of a vehicle already travelling inside the roundabout.

questions.explanation: This is Article 35-2 paragraph 1 of the Road Traffic Act. At a roundabout you keep to the left of the road and proceed slowly along the outer edge whether you are turning right or left.
questions.question: When you turn right at a roundabout you must first keep as far to the left of the road as you can and proceed slowly (徐行) along the outer edge of the roundabout.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Article 37-2 paragraph 1 of the Road Traffic Act you must not obstruct the progress of a vehicle already travelling inside the roundabout, and the order in which vehicles reached the entrance makes no difference.
questions.question: Even if a vehicle is travelling inside the roundabout, you may go straight in as long as your own vehicle reached the entrance first.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(3). You then release the handbrake and let the brake pedal up gradually.
questions.question: To move off you keep the brake pedal firmly pressed, put the selector into D to go forward or R to reverse, and look to confirm the position is right.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(3). It is a danger peculiar to automatic vehicles.
questions.question: If you work the selector lever without pressing the brake pedal firmly, the car may leap forward or suddenly reverse.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(2) you start after confirming that the lever is in P.
questions.question: To start the engine of an automatic vehicle you put the selector lever in D.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 5 Section 9 item 1(5) you apply the handbrake firmly first and then select P.
questions.question: To park you put the selector into P first and then apply the handbrake.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(2). One train having gone by does not by itself mean it is safe.
questions.question: Even after a train has passed from one direction, another can be coming from the opposite direction right behind it, so take particular care.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(3). Even a barrier that has only started to descend bars you.
questions.question: You must not enter a railway crossing while the alarm is sounding or the barrier is down or beginning to come down.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(4) you must come to a complete stop (一時停止) and check even when following.
questions.question: When following the vehicle ahead across a railway crossing you need not stop, since that vehicle has already checked.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 1 item 1(5) you avoid stalling by not changing gear and crossing in one go in low gear.
questions.question: Inside a railway crossing it is best to shift up to a higher gear partway so as to get across faster.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(4). Using the foot brake too often on a long descent can make the brakes suddenly stop working.
questions.question: On a downhill stretch you use a low gear to make good use of the engine brake and avoid relying too heavily on the foot brake.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 2(1). Turning the wheel at speed, or braking while turning it, makes the vehicle prone to rolling over or sliding sideways.
questions.question: As you approach a bend or a curve you reduce speed sufficiently on the straight section before it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(6), because moving off uphill is difficult, the vehicle going down gives way to the one coming up.
questions.question: When vehicles pass each other on a hill, the one going up gives way to the one coming down.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 6 Section 2 item 1(3) you must proceed slowly (徐行) near the crest of a hill, and overtaking there is prohibited whatever the view.
questions.question: Near the crest of a hill you may overtake the vehicle ahead once you have confirmed that the view ahead is clear.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 2. A safety helmet should carry the PS(c) mark or the JIS mark.
questions.question: A construction safety helmet is not a motorcycle safety helmet.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 1(1)(b). The others are putting it on its centre stand and wheeling it in a figure of eight.
questions.question: Being able to touch the ground with the toes of both feet when sitting astride is one of the things to check when choosing a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 2 you must not ride a motorcycle without a safety helmet.
questions.question: You need not wear a safety helmet for a short ride to somewhere nearby.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 1 item 2 a construction safety helmet is not a motorcycle safety helmet.
questions.question: A construction safety helmet protects the head too, so it may be used in place of a motorcycle helmet.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 2 item (1). Holding the machine with your body is what keeps it stable.
questions.question: In the correct riding position the arch of the foot rests on the peg with the sole roughly level, the toes point straight ahead, and both knees grip the tank.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 2 item (2). Relax the shoulders and bend the elbows slightly.
questions.question: On a motorcycle you drop the wrists and hold the grips lightly, as though pushing the handlebars forward.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 1(2). You slow down well beforehand on the straight leading into the curve.
questions.question: To take a curve on a motorcycle you lean the machine so that it turns naturally, rather than steering with the handlebars.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 1(3). In the second half of the curve you check that the way ahead is clear and then accelerate a little.
questions.question: Through a curve you adjust speed with the throttle and keep engine power on the wheels rather than disengaging the clutch.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 4 item 1. You combine them to suit the situation.
questions.question: A motorcycle has three ways of braking: the front brake worked by the lever, the rear brake worked by the pedal or a lever, and the engine brake from closing the throttle or changing down.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 4 item 2(1). Unless you hold your riding position you will be pitched forward.
questions.question: To brake on a motorcycle you hold the machine upright with the handlebars straight and apply the front and rear brakes together while the engine brake is working.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 1(2) you lean the machine so that it turns naturally.
questions.question: To take a curve on a motorcycle you turn by steering with the handlebars rather than leaning the machine.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 3 item 1(3) you keep the clutch engaged so that engine power stays on the wheels.
questions.question: Taking a curve on a motorcycle is steadier if you pull in the clutch and coast through.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 4 item 2(1) you brake with the machine upright and the handlebars straight.
questions.question: It does not matter if you brake on a motorcycle while the machine is leaned over and the handlebars are turned.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 4 item 1 there are three, the third being the engine brake from closing the throttle or changing down.
questions.question: A motorcycle has two ways of braking: the front brake and the rear brake.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Kyosoku Chapter 8 Section 2 item (4) you straighten your back and look well ahead.
questions.question: In the correct riding position you straighten your back and look just in front of the front wheel.

questions.explanation: This is Article 84 paragraph 5 of the Road Traffic Act. There is no provisional licence for motorcycles or mopeds.
questions.question: Provisional licences come in four kinds: large vehicle, medium vehicle, semi-medium vehicle and ordinary vehicle.

questions.explanation: This is Article 87 paragraph 1 of the Road Traffic Act. Neither practice nor a test may be driven without one.
questions.question: Anyone who wants to drive a large, medium, semi-medium or ordinary vehicle for practice or for a test without holding a licence for it must obtain the provisional licence matching that class.

questions.explanation: This is Article 87 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act. The seat beside the driver is where that person must sit.
questions.question: Someone practising on a provisional licence must carry a qualified person in the seat beside the driver's seat and drive under their instruction.

questions.explanation: This is Article 87 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act. Periods during which the licence was suspended do not count towards those years.
questions.question: A Class 1 licence holder supervising provisional-licence practice must have held that licence for three years or more in total.

questions.explanation: This is Article 87 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act. For a Class 1 holder the condition is three years or more of holding the licence.
questions.question: Where the person supervising provisional-licence practice holds a Class 2 licence, they must be 21 or over.

questions.explanation: This is Article 88 paragraph 1 item 1 of the Road Traffic Act. Among motorcycle licences, the large one is set at 18.
questions.question: The ordinary motorcycle, small special vehicle and moped licences are not granted to anyone under 16.

questions.explanation: This is Article 88 paragraph 1 item 1 of the Road Traffic Act. For persons specified by Cabinet Order the age is 19.
questions.question: A large vehicle licence is, as a rule, not granted to anyone under 21.

questions.explanation: This is Article 96 paragraph 1 of the Road Traffic Act. The requirements must be met by the time you sit the test.
questions.question: Someone who does not meet the age and other requirements for a licence may not sit the Class 1 driving test.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Article 84 paragraph 5 of the Road Traffic Act there are only four: large, medium, semi-medium and ordinary vehicle.
questions.question: Provisional licences also include ones for large and ordinary motorcycles.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Article 87 paragraph 2 of the Road Traffic Act an ordinary vehicle provisional licence covers ordinary vehicles.
questions.question: Someone with an ordinary vehicle provisional licence may drive a semi-medium vehicle for practice.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Article 88 paragraph 1 item 1 of the Road Traffic Act an ordinary licence is not granted to anyone under 18.
questions.question: An ordinary licence is not granted to anyone under 16.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Article 88 paragraph 1 item 1 of the Road Traffic Act it is not granted to anyone under 18. Sixteen applies to the ordinary motorcycle licence and the like.
questions.question: A large motorcycle licence is not granted to anyone under 16.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. Under Article 87 paragraph 1 of the Road Traffic Act a provisional licence matching the class of vehicle is required for a skills test as well.
questions.question: No provisional licence is needed to drive an ordinary vehicle in a skills test at a designated driving school.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 4. It is different from the marking that prohibits parking only.
questions.question: This road marking prohibits both stopping and parking.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 7. It is the No entry zone, and you must not go into it.
questions.question: This road marking designates a part of the road that vehicles must not use.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 8. It is the No stopping zone, laid out in front of police and fire stations and similar places.
questions.question: This road marking shows a part that vehicles and streetcars (trams) must not enter when congestion means they might end up stopped in it.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. The marking in Kyosoku Appendix 3(2) item 5 prohibits parking only; stopping is allowed.
questions.question: This road marking prohibits both stopping and parking.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 13. A crossing that involves a right turn is prohibited even when you are entering premises off the road.
questions.question: Where this sign stands a vehicle must not cross the road, except for a crossing that involves a left turn in order to enter or leave premises off the road.

questions.explanation: This is Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 15. Overtaking itself is prohibited by the No overtaking sign.
questions.question: Where this sign stands you must not cross onto the right-hand side of the road in order to overtake, but overtaking without crossing onto the right-hand side is not prohibited.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. This sign, Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 7, means the road is closed to motorcycles and general motorized bicycles (mopeds).
questions.question: This sign means that bicycles may not pass.

questions.explanation: This is wrong. This sign, Kyosoku Appendix 3(1) item 14, prohibits U-turns; crossing the road is prohibited by the No crossing for vehicles sign.
questions.question: This sign means that vehicles must not cross the road.
